chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim narrated from Ali ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
I asked my brother Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) about whether the Muhrim (person in Ihram) may wear a garment saturated with saffron. He said: If there is no perfume in it, there is no harm.
Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: This report is a concession (rukhsah), but leaving it is better.

key_terms.الْعُصْفُر: Saffron, a yellow dye often used for its scent
key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The pilgrim in the state of Ihram
key_terms.رُخْصَةٌ: A concession or permission in legal ruling

ai.seo_question: Can a Muhrim wear clothes dyed with saffron if they are not perfumed?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS) clarifies that wearing saffron-dyed clothing during Ihram is permissible provided the dye itself is not scented, distinguishing between the natural aroma of the dye and added perfume. Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar’s commentary highlights this as a specific concession (rukhsa), yet emphasizes that voluntary abstention remains superior (afdal), reflecting the Shia emphasis on both legal permissibility and spiritual excellence (ihtiyat and fadl).
